fatal_errors: The proposed 700–900 °C regime is incompatible with the target immersed tribo-corrosion experiments conducted at 25–100 °C; approximately 1100 °C was used only for rapid thermal-shock conditioning.
The stated humid-air/0.1% NaCl environment does not match the low-ionic-strength deionized-water test environment and is internally ambiguous.
The grain-boundary diffusion and stress-induced migration mechanism conflicts with the observed control by depassivation, repassivation, tribo-layer stability, abrasion, and oxide-layer rupture.
The hypothesis omits the matched DS2205 comparator, alumina counter-body, reciprocating geometry, and relevant load and frequency ranges.
The predicted 30%, 25%, and 40% increases are unsupported numerical inventions and miss the observed nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C.
No supporting evidence is cited, and no measurements are proposed to establish enhanced corrosive-species transport or mechanically induced grain-boundary migration.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad topic of coupled wear and corrosion in a multiphase eutectic high-entropy alloy and offers a nominally testable mechanism, but it does not reconstruct the studied system. The target evidence supports a temperature-dependent competition between film removal, repassivation, and tribo-layer mechanical stability, with polishing and minimum wear near 50 °C and disrupted oxidative or third-body wear at 100 °C. It also shows that the HEA retains its L12/B2 structure and outperforms identically conditioned DS2205 by roughly an order of magnitude in wear rate. In contrast, the generated hypothesis substitutes an unrelated high-temperature diffusion mechanism and unsupported conditions and outcomes. Grain-boundary engineering could alter many properties simultaneously, so the proposed comparison would not specifically distinguish grain-boundary transport from passivation, hardness, phase stability, or tribo-layer effects. A valid falsification test would need direct boundary-migration or tracer-transport evidence while independently measuring wear, electrochemical response, and tribo-layer evolution under the matched aqueous sliding conditions.
